_note: General orientation. Rules, documents, fees and deadlines change and depend on your programme and status, so each topic says which parts are checked against an official page and which are not. No fees or deadlines are written here unless an official page states them.

topics.intro: Admission rules depend on your programme (degree, exchange, short course).
steps: Read the instructions from the office that admitted you.
Prepare the requested documents in the format they ask for.
Ask the Admissions Department if anything is unclear.
notes: Document lists differ by programme. The app does not list them because no single official list applies to everyone.

t.vi: Mã số và thẻ sinh viên

topics.intro: You get a student ID number and, in most cases, a student card. Ask where and when to collect it.
steps: Ask the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) when cards are issued.
Bring your passport.
Report a lost card to OSA quickly.

topics.intro: The portal is where you see your timetable, grades and tuition. Your password belongs to you. This app never asks for it.
steps: Sign in with the account your school gave you.
If you cannot sign in, use the official reset option, then ask the Academic Affairs Office.
Do not share your password with anyone, including apps.
notes: The portal address is not listed here because it was not verified.

topics.intro: Registration happens on the official HUST system during a registration window. This app only helps you plan.
steps: Plan your classes in the Course planner and check clashes.
Ask your school or the Academic Affairs Office for the registration dates.
Register on the official system.
Check the result there. Do not rely on this app.
notes: The TKB file shows classes with status 'Điều chỉnh ĐK' (adjustment), 'Đăng ký' (open), 'Kết thúc ĐK' (closed) or 'Huỷ lớp' (cancelled).

topics.applies: Depends on your programme and scholarship
topics.intro: Whether and how much you pay depends on your programme and scholarship. HUST publishes tuition announcements on its news board.
steps: Read the latest tuition announcements (see Home, Official notices).
Ask OSA or your sponsor if your tuition is covered.
Pay only through the method named in the official announcement.
notes: No amount or date is shown here. Use the official announcement.

topics.intro: Some students are funded by a government or home institution. Others apply for HUST scholarships.
steps: Ask your sponsor what they require from you each semester.
Ask OSA about HUST scholarships and the application period.
notes: The project brief says OSA handles scholarship questions.

topics.intro: Regulations cover attendance, study duration, suspending studies, changing majors and discipline.
steps: Ask your school office for the current regulations for your programme.
Ask before you suspend studies or change major: it can affect your visa and scholarship.
Keep written confirmations.
notes: Discipline levels in the project brief: reprimand, warning, suspension, expulsion. Consequences for international students (including repatriation) should be confirmed with OSA.

topics.intro: Exam rules are set by the university and your school.
steps: Check dates and rooms in the portal and the timetable.
Bring your student card and what the rules allow.
Ask the lecturer if you cannot attend because of illness.

topics.intro: Grades appear in the student portal. The GPA tool in this app is personal and is not an official calculation.
steps: Check grades in the portal.
Ask the lecturer or school first if you disagree.
Ask the Academic Affairs Office about the formal review process.

topics.intro: The Ta Quang Buu Library has reading rooms and specialised collections.
steps: Show your student card at the librarian's desk before entering a reading room.
Reading-room items are used inside the room.
notes: See the Library guide for rooms.

t.vi: Bảo hiểm y tế và khám chữa bệnh

topics.intro: Insurance rules depend on your programme and status. Emergencies come first: call 115.
steps: Ask OSA which insurance applies to you.
Ask where you should go first when you are sick.
Keep your insurance card with your passport copy.
notes: The campus clinic's location and hours are not verified.

topics.intro: HUST states that students coming to study must hold a study visa. Tourist or visiting-relatives visas are not accepted.
steps: Visa Approval Letter (non-degree students): tell your supervisor, the Admission Office or the international office at least 3 months before departure and submit their online form. HUST says the letter takes 2-3 weeks.
Extension: needs approval from HUST and your home university, or special circumstances such as serious illness. HUST does not extend visas for work, travel or family visits.
Extension documents: your passport with the Vietnam visa and the application form from the international office. Submit at least 1 month before the visa expires.
Late submission can be refused and fined, and a refused extension may require you to leave.
docs: Application form provided by the international office
notes: This page was published on 31/01/2021. Offices and rules may have changed, so confirm with OSA.
Fees follow current Vietnamese regulations. No fee is shown here.
Degree-seeking students: the page does not name a contact. Ask OSA.

topics.intro: The Dormitory Management Center handles dormitory rooms.
steps: Go to B9, rooms 101-102, or call 024 3869 2942.
Ask about room types, rules and how to apply. The official page lists none of these.
notes: No prices or application dates are shown here.

topics.intro: Use Office finder to find the right office for a problem.
steps: Describe your problem in Office finder.
Go to the office listed, or write to the email if one is shown.
Keep a note of who you spoke to.

topics.intro: Graduation steps depend on your programme.
steps: Ask your school office for the graduation requirements and dates.
Ask the Academic Affairs Office about the graduation procedure.
Plan your visa so it covers the final period.
